pages.text: Daniel and his mom moved to a new town, far away from home. There was sun, and palm trees, and a new school. But Daniel did not know anyone.
At the beach, Daniel met a kind girl named Ali. But a big boy named Johnny did not like Daniel. Johnny pushed him down in the sand, and everyone laughed.
Johnny and his friends learned karate at a school called Cobra Kai. Their teacher was strict and mean. "Strike first!" he shouted. "Never say sorry!"
In Daniel's building lived a quiet old man named Mr. Miyagi. He fixed things. He fixed Daniel's broken bike. And he cut tiny trees with tiny scissors. Snip, snip.
On Halloween night, Johnny's gang dressed up as skeletons and chased Daniel. Then, whoosh! Mr. Miyagi jumped over the fence. He moved like the wind, and the big boys all tumbled down.
"Please, teach me karate!" said Daniel. Mr. Miyagi said, "Karate is not for fighting. Karate is for keeping safe." Then he made a deal. Daniel would meet Johnny at the big karate contest.
The next morning, Mr. Miyagi gave Daniel a sponge. "Wax on, right hand. Wax off, left hand." Round and round, Daniel waxed car after car, all day long.
The next day, he sanded the floor. Then he painted the fence, up and down. Then he painted the house, side to side. Daniel's arms were very, very tired.
Daniel got cross. "I came to learn karate, not to do your chores!" Mr. Miyagi said, "Show me wax on!" and he punched. Daniel's hand blocked it! Every chore had been a karate move.
Daniel practised every day. At the beach, he watched Mr. Miyagi stand on one leg, arms up like a bird. "This is the crane," said Mr. Miyagi. "Do it right, and nothing can stop it."
Then came the big contest. Daniel was the smallest, but he was fast. He won one round, then another, then another. Johnny could not believe it.
In the last round, Johnny's teacher told him to play a mean trick. Johnny kicked Daniel's leg on purpose. Daniel fell down. His leg hurt a lot.
Mr. Miyagi rubbed his hands together, fast and warm, and held Daniel's leg. "Can you stand?" Daniel stood up slowly, on one leg... just like a crane.

Johnny ran at him. Daniel jumped, and kicked. Point! Daniel won! Then Johnny gave him the trophy. "You're all right, Daniel." Small practice, every day, made Daniel strong. And it can make you strong too. The end.
